c74object.name: evi.overdrive.wrap~
c74object.digest: Antialiased atan-based saturation with shape input to control overdrive and gain wrapping
c74object.description:
evi.overdrive.wrap~ is a 'max define' for the evi_overdrive_wrap.gendsp gen~ abstraction. Because evi.overdrive.wrap~ is a 'max define' it also accepts all messages and attributes that a gen~ object does.
This atan() overdrive is a simple but deluxe memoryless nonlinear processor with atan() gain wrapping around it's core nonlinearity (controlled via inlet 2) and various antialiasing options. The object can be driven hard and maintains stability and dirty sound. At high gain input the evi.overdrive.wrap~ shape is similar to MSP overdrive~, but is antialiased and clean.

inlet.description: Linear gain 1..100 (0..40 dB). This actually controls a reciprocal gain wrapping around the internal saturator. The object handles high gain very well with minimal aliasing. This inlet corresponds to the equivalent inlet of the MSP 'overdrive~' object.

outlet.digest: Outlet #1: Atan(x) Output - antialiased for your audio not for Maths

outlet.description: A sample accurate reset 'click' whenever the 'aa' or 'hfcompensate' attributes are changed. Might be useful.

attribute.name: aa
attribute.description: The 'aa' ('Anti Aliasing') method used. 0=Adaa1, 1=Adaa1 2x oversampled, 2=Adaa1 4x oversampled, 3=Adaa2 (default), 4=Adaa2 2x oversampled, 5=Adaa2 4x oversampled. 0..5 does not necessarily mean increasing in quality, it really depends on your audio input material.

attribute.name: hfcompensate
attribute.description: The object provides a high frequency compensation 'decorelation' filter on its output for restoring the reduced high frequency response that can occur with this type of antialiasing, especially when utilising the oversampling options (as opposed to just using pure 'adaa'). Experiment with turning this on to improve high frequencies (default on).

c74object.discussion: For more information about evieve Overdrive processors and other saturation types see the 'evieve overdrive' tab of the helpfile.
